conventions.convention: Indices start at 1. Parameters are real square-summable sequences. Contraction concerns a specified posterior version, under the fixed-truth data law, as positive noise ε decreases to zero.
A positive rε tending to zero is a contraction rate when expected posterior mass outside Mεrε tends to zero for every positive Mε tending to infinity.

The theorem uses unnormalized observations Yj = sjθj + εξj; these are obtained by multiplying the sequence model's normalized observations by sj > 0. AC and Countable Choice are assumed, and every prior coordinate variance is strictly positive with finite total variance.
The counterexample permits a degenerate centered Gaussian prior, specifically δ0, and uses truth e1. Its fixed-truth and prior-predictive data laws are equivalent at every positive noise level.

load_bearing.statement: Assume AC and Countable Choice, ε > 0, positive singular values from the Gaussian sequence inverse model, truth θ† ∈ ℓ², and an independent-coordinate Gaussian Borel prior with τj > 0 and Σjτj² < ∞, independent of observation noise. Put vj = (τj⁻² + sj²/ε²)⁻¹ and λj = τj²sj²/(ε² + τj²sj²). A posterior version is, fixed-truth-almost surely, the ℓ² restriction of the product of N(λjYj/sj, vj). Its expected posterior squared error equals Σj[(1−λj)²(θ†j)² + vj²sj²/ε² + vj], which is finite. Expected posterior mass outside radius R > 0 is at most this sum divided by R². Consequently Sε(θ†) ≤ Crε² with positive rε → 0 implies contraction at rate rε.

For supplied proper Borel priors and specified posterior kernels in the Gaussian sequence inverse experiment, a positive function rε → 0 is a posterior contraction rate at fixed θ† ∈ ℓ² if, for every positive Mε → ∞, the fixed-truth expectation of posterior mass on {θ : ‖θ−θ†‖₂ > Mεrε} tends to zero as ε ↓ 0.

seams_checked.note: The inherited white-noise coordinates are independent normal observations at positive noise. No Hilbert-valued white-noise sample or simultaneous path identity is assumed.
The real ℓ² parameter, positive singular values and product-Borel sample space agree. The theorem explicitly obtains its unnormalized Y coordinates by multiplying normalized Z coordinates by sj.

This is contextual. The assigned items do not invoke minimax optimality or identify a contraction upper bound with an order-sharp minimax result. The exponential example explicitly identifies the minimax source as context only.

The assigned definition supplies a posterior kernel and records its version limitation. The infinite-product posterior is constructed directly, without assuming an infinite-dimensional Lebesgue likelihood or applying finite-evidence propriety beyond its hypotheses.

Scalar and finite-block conditioning use positive noise covariance and the exact supplied Gaussian mean/covariance formulas. Infinite-product support and kernel measurability are established separately.
The open-problem item's reference describes precisely the expected-tail, diverging-multiplier contraction convention. It does not infer frequentist coverage from contraction.
